superseded_note: SUPERSEDED IN PART by data/fascicle34_tei_verified_pairs.json, which uses the actual manuscript TEI markup (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10316549) instead of secondary reading-edition text. Three corrections that file documents: (1) the poem-3 'vehicle'/'Curricle' pair had its base/variant direction backwards here -- correct direction is base 'Curricle' -> variant 'Vehicle'; (2) the poem-6 'should'->'could' pair was a misreading -- the actual marked pair is base 'Would' -> variant 'Could -', a different word; (3) the poem-11 'Root'->'Core' pair below is RETRACTED -- the TEI shows no variant markup at 'Root' at all; that was an unconfirmed inference, not a verified reading. The 'time'->'Day' (poem 5) and 'exorbitant'->'Extravagant'/'importunate' (poem 6) pairs below remain valid as the team's own hand-observation, but are confirmed ABSENT from this project's scraped TEI files -- see the missing_markup_finding in the newer file.
purpose: First-pass classification of newly verified base-text/variant pairs from Fascicle 34 poems the team's 2022 worked example never covered. Unlike round 1 (fascicle34_worked_example_ground_truth.json), there is no team-assigned category to validate against here -- the team never formally classified these poems. This is new classification, not a validation test.
verification_method: Each base text was confirmed against a published reading-edition text of the poem (found via web search, sourced to Wikisource/standard poetry databases), matched against the position/context clues in the team's own 2022 Fascicle 34 documentation (data/fascicle34_hand_coding.json). Only pairs confirmable this way are included -- several poems' remaining variants were left out because Dickinson's manuscripts often interleave variants within a line in ways that can't be reconstructed without the actual manuscript image (see PLAN.md).

pairs.poem: A little Road- not made of Man
pairs.verification: Reading text: 'If town it have, beyond itself'
pairs.reason: "Besides" and "beyond" both signal something apart from the road itself; the variant restates rather than changes the base meaning.

pairs.poem: A little Road- not made of Man
pairs.verification: Reading text: 'no vehicle / Bears me along that way'; team's own note explains what a curricle is
pairs.reason: "Curricle" sharpens the generic "vehicle" into a vivid, specific conveyance, intensifying the image.

pairs.poem: Pain- has an Element of Blank
pairs.verification: Reading text: 'A time when it was not'
pairs.reason: "Day" concretizes the abstract "time"; neither repeats, amplifies, opposes, nor adds content.

pairs.verification: Reading text: 'Too exorbitant / To the Lady'
pairs.reason: "Extravagant" is a near-synonym of "exorbitant" describing the same excess.
"Importunate" shifts sense from excessive-in-degree to excessively demanding -- a different quality, not a repetition or amplification.
"Could" trades obligatory/likely force for mere possibility -- a modal shift, not repetition/amplification/antithesis.
"Core" intensifies "Root" by moving from the tree's literal anchor to its essential center.

pairs.verification: Reading text: 'Best Horizon-gone-'; team's own note: 'There's a gulf between gone and known'
pairs.reason: "Known" directly contradicts "gone" (presence/recognition vs. loss); the poem's imagery of severance and destroyed future favors "gone" as the coherent reading.

pairs.poem: My Life had stood- a Loaded Gun
pairs.verification: Reading text: 'For I have but the art to kill - / Without the power to die'; already worked through in the team's own 2022 paper draft as a dictionary-alignment example, but never assigned a formal category
pairs.reason: Swapping "art" for "power" interrogates whether the gun's relation to killing/dying is skill/agency versus raw capacity -- the poem's own unresolved paradox about instrumentality.

note_on_recurring_pattern: 3 of these 9 pairs (33%) independently drew the 'Substitutive (undefined)' label from the classifying agent, with no knowledge of the earlier round-1 result. Combined with round 1 (9 of 16 team-labeled pairs, 56%, used the team's own undefined 'Substitutive' label), this is now two independent pieces of evidence that plain substitution is the taxonomy's single largest blind spot, not a one-off artifact of the first test.
